title: bb_visualize: a target is a VALUE — %, _ and \ match themselves

checks.name: control: a plain module target resolves
control: `src/util` does not bleed into `src/utilities`
control: the segment boundary is exact (src/utilities is a different module)
underscore: module target with `_` resolves (was 0 before the escape clause)
underscore: and is NOT declared absent against the project
underscore: the module's own file is returned
underscore: a snake_case feature target resolves (was 0 before)
underscore: the named symbol is in the answer
underscore: file scope resolves it by equality as well
underscore: a different spelling does not match `my_mod` [negative]
percent: a module whose NAME contains % and _ resolves
percent: the symbol under that directory is returned
percent: the answer is not an absence note about an existing module [negative]
percent is literal: `src/util%` matches nothing
percent is literal: the miss is declared with the target verbatim [negative]
checks.detail: no indexed symbol matches scope=module target="src/util%" — absence declared, never guessed

checks.name: percent is literal: `100%` matches the docstring that contains it
percent is literal: the docstring's symbol is the one returned
percent is literal: `1%0` does not match `100%` (a wildcard would) [negative]
backslash: a target containing the escape character does not throw
backslash: and does not widen into a match (the escape character is itself escapable) [negative]
trailing slash: a directory target with a trailing slash behaves like one without

decisions.metacharacters: a real directory is named `src/50%_util`, so matching it proves both characters match themselves
decisions.wildcardNegatives: `src/util%` and `feature 1%0` return nothing — both WOULD match if % were a wildcard
decisions.absence: an empty answer names the target verbatim, so a declared absence is checkable

limitations: No fixture file can contain a backslash on every platform, so the backslash case is asserted as a non-match that does not throw or widen.
Case-folding of targets and the rejection of unknown languages/relationship types (F6/F7) are the next batch.
